title: Payments Operations Calendar Convention: Payment Channel and the Extended Hardship Settlement Due Day
content:
# Hardship Settlement — Payment-Channel Convention for Extended Due Dates

The channel of the most recent consumer payment in the money history of the Placed Consumer Accounts record decides the weekday treatment of a due date extended under a Hardship Settlement of Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements.

**Convention.** The Hardship Settlement payment-channel convention decides on which day the extended first payment falls: where the most recent consumer payment posted to the account, a payment later returned included, came by ACH bank debit, an extended due date that falls on a Saturday or a Sunday is moved back to the Friday before it; where it came by mailed check or money order, an extended due date that falls on a Saturday or a Sunday is moved forward to the Monday after it; where it came by any other channel, or no consumer payment is posted, the extended due date stands whatever day of the week it falls on.

The days of the extension follow the move: a move back to the Friday gives fewer days, a move forward to the Monday gives more.

## Channel table

| Most recent consumer payment posted to the account | Extended due date on a Saturday or Sunday |
|---|---|
| ACH bank debit | moved back to the Friday before it |
| mailed check | moved forward to the Monday after it |
| money order | moved forward to the Monday after it |
| any other channel, such as a card | stands |
| no consumer payment posted | stands |

An extended due date that falls Monday to Friday stands under every channel.

## Hypothetical cases

1. Most recent payment by ACH bank debit, later returned; a 9-day extension would land on a Sunday: the due date moves back to the Friday, 7 days.
2. Most recent payment by mailed check; a 6-day extension would land on a Saturday: moved forward to the Monday, 8 days.
3. Most recent payment by debit card; an extension landing on a Saturday stands.
